messages:
maya: quick summary of the A100 vs H100 sweep I ran today across mosaic-7b and starcoder-7b in us-east1 / us-west2 / eu-west1. paste of key numbers + notes below. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: nice, what was the exact test harness/config?

maya: harness: ./bench --model <model> --quant int8 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --prefill 1024 --decode 512 --warmup 200 --samples 1000 --export-csv=out.csv

maya: command examples (used per-gpu pinned runs):
```
# mosaic on A100
./bench --model mosaic-7b --device a100 --quant int8 --seq 2048 --prefill 1024 --decode 512
# mosaic on H100
./bench --model mosaic-7b --device h100 --quant int8 --seq 2048 --prefill 1024 --decode 512
```

maya: results (median across 3 runs, tokens/sec = total tokens processed per second across prefill+decode; prefill/decode are median lat in ms):
- mosaic-7b (A100, int8): tokens/sec 18,200, prefill 118 ms, decode 9.2 ms/token, $/1M tokens ~$29.5
- mosaic-7b (H100, int8): tokens/sec 25,400, prefill 92 ms, decode 6.6 ms/token, $/1M tokens ~$22.1
- starcoder-7b (A100, int8): tokens/sec 15,500, prefill 140 ms, decode 10.1 ms/token, $/1M tokens ~$33.0
- starcoder-7b (H100, int8): tokens/sec 21,600, prefill 108 ms, decode 7.3 ms/token, $/1M tokens ~$25.6

yuki: did you force kernel selection or let the runtime pick? any fp16 fallbacks observed?

maya: runtime auto-picked. H100 picked optimized int8 attention kernels (AMX-ish path) consistently. A100 hit a fallback to fp16_attention on ~4% of long requests in one run (memory path mismatch) — saw increase in prefill latency in that run. snippet from kernel log: 

```
[info] kernel-selection: int8_attention -> OK
[warn] kernel-selection: int8_attention -> fallback fp16_attention (reason: mem-layout mismatch)
```

igor: region differences? pricing or perf delta?

maya: perf by region: us-east ~= us-west within noise (+/- 3%), eu-west decode latency ~+7% on both skus (likely instance micro-arch/placement). cost: eu-west A100 rental premium pushed $/1M tokens +6% there. H100 stayed cheaper per token even after regional pricing.

sam: quality check on int8? any regressions on downstream evals?

maya: ran quick evals on heldout dialog set (rouge / task-specific metrics): mosaic-7b int8 delta negligible (<=0.1% metric drift). starcoder-7b int8 showed a small tokenization/perplexity drift on long-context (>1500 tokens) cases (~0.4% perplexity increase). marking for full eval and human spot-check.

yuki: can you upload artifacts? charts + raw csvs?

ci-bot: benchmark artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-bench/1712345678/ (out.csv, charts/, kernel-logs.txt) :white_check_mark:

maya: quick sizing note for Dedicated pools (ballpark): for mosaic-7b, typical request = 200 tokens average. at 500 rps -> tokens/sec = 100k tps. using measured H100 throughput (25.4k tps) -> ~4 GPUs required (100k/25.4k = 3.94) => plan 5 GPUs per zone to allow headroom and failover. using A100 throughput (18.2k tps) -> ~6 GPUs -> plan 7 with buffer.

sam: nice, that's helpful for capacity planning. any microburst behavior?

maya: microburst: when we hit many concurrent small requests, batching improves decode throughput but increases tail latency. observed ~12% tail latency spike at sudden 2x traffic - mitigations: aggressive per-request priority routing + small dynamic cache for prefix KV reduces spikes.

yuki: next experiments?

maya: plan: 24h steady-state 500 qps run, test 6-bit quant on H100 (we've seen promising perf in internal sim), and attempt kernel pinning to prevent fp16 fallback on A100. will also run full eval sweep for starcoder long-context cases.

sam: can you paste the perf CSV when ready?

maya: yes, will dump out.csv and link here when done. provisional dashboard: https://dash.redwood/infer/bench/1712345678 (charts + region breakdown).

igor: thanks. this will feed the Dedicated SKU sizing doc. :thumbsup:

maya: cool, I'll follow up with the 24h artifacts. ping me if you want the raw kernel logs or run configs earlier.

sam: ack, thanks maya.
